payload.task_text:
I need an analysis of quiz performance for the course "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics" which is offered in Fall 2013 and has a course ID of 3 in the learning management system. (The course's exact name in the LMS is "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)"; use the course ID 3 to look it up.) Please look up all quizzes for this course and gather the submission data for each quiz.

Create an Excel file called Quiz_Performance.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be called "Quiz Stats" with columns Quiz_Title, Total_Submissions, Avg_Score (rounded to 2 decimal places), Min_Score, Max_Score, and Pass_Rate (the percentage of submissions scoring 60 or above, rounded to 2 decimal places). Sort the rows by quiz title.

The second sheet should be called "Summary" with two columns Metric and Value. Include the following rows: Total_Quizzes (the number of distinct quizzes), Overall_Avg_Score (the average score across all submissions in all quizzes for this course, rounded to 2 decimal places), Highest_Avg_Quiz (the title of the quiz with the highest average score), and Lowest_Avg_Quiz (the title of the quiz with the lowest average score).

After creating the Excel file, send a summary email to instructor@university.example.com from quiz-analytics@university.example.com with the subject "Quiz Performance Summary - Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)". The email body should include the total number of quizzes analyzed, the overall average score, and the names of the highest and lowest performing quizzes.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must complete this small five-quiz task directly; do not dispatch any sub-agent. The five-row table supplies exact fields to the quiz procedure below.

Email-owner contract for every email sub-task below: call `search_emails(query=<literal subject>, folder="Sent", page=<n>, page_size=50)` from page 1 through the returned final page. Because search results do not expose recipients, call `read_email(email_id=<candidate id>)` for every candidate and match the complete literal `To`, `Subject`, and, whenever the Task specifies it, `From`; a subject-only hit is not a match. Call `send_email` exactly once only when no exact match exists. After sending, repeat the paginated search, call `read_email` on every candidate, require exactly one exact match, and return its ID plus exact recipient/sender/subject/body read-back. If search, send, or read-back fails, return a blocker and do not retry `send_email`.

**Quiz procedure.** Call `canvas_list_quiz_submissions(course_id=3, quiz_id=<quiz_id>)` exactly once; the response is complete and unpaginated. Treat this endpoint only as score evidence, and obtain `quiz_title` and `points_possible` only from the `canvas_list_quizzes` inventory. For numeric scores compute `score_sum`, `score_min`, `score_max`, and `pass_count_ge_60`; define every submission identity and duplicate check from literal `row.id`. Do not modify Canvas.

The main agent performs these seven independent read-only operations directly in one native-parallel tool-call response:

   1. Call `canvas_get_course(course_id=3)` exactly once. Return `{course_id,course_code,course_name,total_students,identity_ok,call_count,warnings}` and require exact name `Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)`. Do not call quizzes or submissions.

   2. Call `canvas_list_quizzes(course_id=3)` exactly once. Return every quiz as `{quiz_id,title,points_possible}`, sorted by quiz ID, plus `returned_count`, unique IDs, and warnings. Require the exact manifest `6:CMA 15003, 7:CMA 15004, 8:CMA 15005, 9:CMA 15006, 10:CMA 15007`; do not call submissions.

   Apply the quiz procedure to these exact rows:

| row_no | course_id | quiz_id | quiz_title |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 3 | 6 | CMA 15003 |
| 2 | 3 | 7 | CMA 15004 |
| 3 | 3 | 8 | CMA 15005 |
| 4 | 3 | 9 | CMA 15006 |
| 5 | 3 | 10 | CMA 15007 |

The main agent verifies course identity, requires the five-row inventory exactly once, joins title and points exclusively from that inventory, and derives the task metrics with the stated denominators and deterministic tie-break.

It then starts the workbook-create/write branch and the exact sent-mail search in the same native-parallel response; neither branch waits for the other. Workbook read-back and the email's conditional send/read-back continue independently. It performs both outputs directly:

   1. Resolve the runtime workspace root and own `Quiz_Performance.xlsx` there exactly once. Create `Quiz Stats(Quiz_Title,Total_Submissions,Avg_Score,Min_Score,Max_Score,Pass_Rate)` with exactly five title-sorted rows and two-decimal averages/rates, and `Summary(Metric,Value)` with exactly `Total_Quizzes`, `Overall_Avg_Score`, `Highest_Avg_Quiz`, and `Lowest_Avg_Quiz`. Write literal values, not formulas. Read both sheets back and return `{path,hash,sheets:[{name,headers,row_count}],quiz_titles,stored_summary,arithmetic_checks,verification}`. Do not send email.

   2. Own only one email from `quiz-analytics@university.example.com` to `instructor@university.example.com` with subject `Quiz Performance Summary - Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)`. Follow the Email-owner contract above. Search the exact sender/recipient/subject first; if absent, call `send_email(to="instructor@university.example.com", from_addr="quiz-analytics@university.example.com", subject="Quiz Performance Summary - Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)", body=<verified total quiz count, overall average, complete highest title, complete lowest title>)` once; if present, do not duplicate it. Read back or search again and return `{message_id,from,to,subject,total_quizzes,overall_average,highest_title,lowest_title,action,duplicate_count,verification}`. Do not modify files.

Finally, reconcile the five source summaries, two workbook sheets, and one email. Verify quiz identity/order, denominators, rounding, literal workbook values, full highest/lowest titles, sender/recipient/subject/body values, read-back evidence, and absence of a duplicate message before claiming completion.

nodes.text:
You are a planning sub-agent. Please decompose the following task into ordered subtasks and return a plan. Do NOT execute any write/mutation operations — plan only (you may use read-only tools to inspect the environment if helpful, e.g. check what files exist in the workspace).

TASK DESCRIPTION:
1. In a Canvas LMS instance, look up the course with ID 3, whose exact name is "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)" (also referred to as "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics", Fall 2013 term).
2. Look up ALL quizzes in this course and gather the submission data for each quiz (each submission's score).
3. Create an Excel file named Quiz_Performance.xlsx in the workspace (workspace dir: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-quiz-performance-excel/workspace) with two sheets:
   - Sheet 1 named "Quiz Stats" with columns: Quiz_Title, Total_Submissions, Avg_Score (rounded to 2 decimal places), Min_Score, Max_Score, Pass_Rate (percentage of submissions scoring 60 or above, rounded to 2 decimal places). Rows sorted by quiz title.
   - Sheet 2 named "Summary" with columns: Metric, Value. Rows: Total_Quizzes (number of distinct quizzes), Overall_Avg_Score (average score across ALL submissions in all quizzes for this course, rounded to 2 decimal places), Highest_Avg_Quiz (title of the quiz with the highest average score), Lowest_Avg_Quiz (title of the quiz with the lowest average score).
4. Send an email to instructor@university.example.com FROM quiz-analytics@university.example.com with subject "Quiz Performance Summary - Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)". The email body must include: total number of quizzes analyzed, the overall average score, and the names of the highest and lowest performing quizzes.

AVAILABLE TOOLS (context): Canvas MCP tools (list_quizzes, list_quiz_submissions, get_quiz, get_course, etc.), Excel MCP tools (create_workbook, create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, read_data_from_excel, etc.), email MCP tools (send_email, etc.), filesystem tools, and local python execution.

For each subtask, specify:
- The dispatch decision: self (main agent), explore, or coder.
- Whether the subtask is independent of its siblings (parallelizable) or must wait for another subtask's output.
- Any risks/edge cases to watch (e.g. quiz submissions may include ungraded/empty scores, quiz scores may be nil for unsubmitted attempts, Excel formatting of percentages, sorting by title, etc.).

Return a concise, ordered plan with clear subtasks.
Plan quiz performance analysis task

You are a read-only exploration sub-agent. Goal: characterize the quiz submission data for Canvas course 3 so that quiz statistics can be computed consistently. Do NOT modify anything in Canvas or on disk — read-only queries only.

CONTEXT:
- Course id: 3, name "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)".
- The course has exactly 5 quizzes (already enumerated): id 6 "CMA 15003", id 7 "CMA 15004", id 8 "CMA 15005", id 9 "CMA 15006", id 10 "CMA 15007". Scoring policy is keep_highest; allowed attempts vary (1-3).
- Use the tool mcp__canvas__canvas_list_quiz_submissions(course_id=3, quiz_id=N) for each quiz N in 6..10. The payloads are large; if the tool supports pagination parameters (per_page/page) or preview options, use them sensibly, but you must determine the TOTAL number of records per quiz.

FOR EACH QUIZ (6,7,8,9,10), report:
1. Total number of submission records returned.
2. JSON structure: list the field names of a sample submission record and show one example record (truncate if huge).
3. Whether multiple records can share the same user_id (i.e., one record per attempt vs one per user): give count of unique user_ids vs total records.
4. workflow_state values and their counts.
5. The score field: its type (string/number/null), 10 sample values, and the count of records with null/empty score.
6. kept_score field: present? sample values? count of nulls?
7. attempt field: sample values.
8. Whether scores look like percentages (0-100 scale) or raw points out of some total (note points_possible is "1.00" on the quiz, but scores observed elsewhere look like "100.00", "80.00").
9. Whether there are any other fields that distinguish a real student submission from previews/auto-generated ones (e.g., 'preview' flag, 'temporary_user_code').

RETURN: a compact structured report with the above, per quiz. Do NOT paste the full payloads — just the summarized facts and small samples.
Explore quiz submission structure

You are computing quiz statistics for Canvas course 3 ("Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)"). You own exactly ONE quiz, identified as: 25 | 6 | CMA 15003 (format: assignment_id | quiz_id | quiz_title).

CONTEXT:
- Course id: 3. The quiz you own is backed by a Canvas assignment whose id is the assignment_id in your item. The quiz id and exact quiz title are also given in your item.
- Submission data is retrieved via the bulk submissions endpoint which supports server-side pagination.

YOUR TASKS:
1. Fetch ALL submissions for your assignment: call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_student_submissions with course_id=3, assignment_ids=[<assignment_id>], student_ids=["all"], per_page=100, page=1. The response contains a "submissions" array and a "pagination" object with fields total_count, total_pages, has_more. Keep calling with increasing page numbers (page=2, 3, ...) until pagination.has_more is false. Collect the FULL set of submission records — do not stop early.
2. For every submission record, extract the score: the "score" field is a string such as "100.00" or "60.00" on a 0-100 percentage scale. Convert to float. Include every record that has a non-null numeric score (all records in this dataset are graded/complete). Sanity check: the response also includes "assignment_name" — verify it matches your quiz title.
3. Compute, using ALL collected scores:
   - total_submissions = number of score records
   - avg_score = sum/count, rounded to 2 decimal places
   - min_score, max_score
   - pass_count = number of scores >= 60; pass_rate = pass_count / total_submissions * 100, rounded to 2 decimal places
   - score_sum = sum of all scores (unrounded) and score_count = count (needed for an overall course average later)
4. Do NOT modify anything in Canvas and do NOT create any files. This is read-only computation.

RETURN in your final message EXACTLY this JSON (no extra commentary):
{"quiz_title": "<exact quiz title>", "total_submissions": <int>, "avg_score": <float 2dp>, "min_score": <float>, "max_score": <float>, "pass_rate": <float 2dp>, "score_sum": <float>, "score_count": <int>}
Fetch submissions and compute per-quiz stats
